extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and legal practitioners subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO final disciplinary order resolving a disciplinary complaint by stipulated facts and a proposed settlement under USPTO regulations; sets jurisdictional bases, the misconduct found, and the agreed sanction (public reprimand) and publication/notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO registration and applicability of disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant hereto, Respondent ... has been an attorney registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office ('USPTO' or 'the Office') and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20g g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that USPTO-registered practitioners are subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility; registration number is recorded (here, 47,166).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director jurisdictional basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(A) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3) and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies statutory and regulatory authority under which the Director may adjudicate or approve settlement of disciplinary matters affecting registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary findings can constitute USPTO rule violation (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by being disciplined on ethical grounds by the Indiana Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination or discipline by a state disciplinary authority for ethical misconduct may be treated as a violation of USPTO professional responsibility rules and may form the basis for USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Settlement Agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. §11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent's Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions ... The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements must set out stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and must satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to resolve related USPTO disciplinary claims voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulated facts must support discipline (example of misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2004, Respondent represented a doctor in the dissolution of a medical practice ... Respondent wrote directly to the other doctor three times. The third time was after the other doctor's attorney asked Respondent not to communicate directly with the other doctor. On or about September 12, 2008, Respondent ... conditionally agreed in writing that Respondent violated Indiana Professional Conduct Rule 4.2 by directly contacting a party who Respondent knew to be represented by another lawyer ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete factual admissions (e.g., direct communications with a party known to be represented despite opposing counsel's instruction) are used as the factual basis for disciplinary findings and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction imposed — public reprimand and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded; The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette: 'Notice of Reprimand' ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary remedies may include a public reprimand and mandatory publication of the reprimand in the Official Gazette and OED materials; the order may specify exact publication and notice actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content and dissemination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice in the Official Gazette describes: name, location, registration number, that the practitioner has been reprimanded by the USPTO for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) for engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice before the Office, specifics of the underlying state reprimand, statutory/regulatory citations (35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(A) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3), 11.26 and 11.59), and reference to OED Reading Room availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires the OED Director to give notice of public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public; it may include a specific wording template and link for the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements commonly specify how costs are allocated between the parties (here, each party bears its own costs).
